webhooks.name: clusterservingruntime.kserve-webhook-server.validator
webhooks.purpose: Validates ServingRuntime and ClusterServingRuntime resources on create/update to ensure model format priority consistency (no duplicate priorities across runtimes for the same model format and protocol, and consistent priorities within a single runtime), and validates multi-node worker spec constraints including GPU resource types, parallel size values, blocked environment variables, and disallowing removal of an existing workerSpec.

webhooks.name: inferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.pod-mutator
webhooks.purpose: Mutates pods owned by KServe InferenceServices at creation time, injecting storage initializer init-containers (for model downloading with appropriate credentials), inference logger/batcher agent sidecars, metrics aggregator sidecars, GKE accelerator node selectors, Istio CNI security contexts, and optionally modelcar (OCI image source) volumes. It reads the InferenceService config and credential secrets to configure these injected containers.

name: llminferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha1.defaulter
purpose: Mutating defaulter that applies defaults to LLMInferenceService resources and, when local model caching is enabled in the inference service ConfigMap, lists cluster-scoped LocalModelCache and namespace-scoped LocalModelNamespaceCache resources to find one whose storage URI matches the service's model URI, then stamps matching local-model labels and PVC-name annotations onto the LLMInferenceService (namespace-scoped caches take precedence over cluster-scoped ones).

name: llminferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha1.validator
purpose: Validating webhook for LLMInferenceService v1alpha1 resources on create and update. It enforces cross-field constraints on router/gateway/HTTPRoute configuration, ensures parallelism settings are consistent (e.g., worker requires parallelism, pipeline and data parallelism are mutually exclusive, data and dataLocal must be paired), validates scheduler config (replicas > 0, inline vs ref exclusivity), delegates scaling validation to the v1alpha2 hub type, and prevents mutation of the total parallelism size on updates.

name: llminferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha2.defaulter
purpose: Mutating defaulter that applies defaults to LLMInferenceService resources and, when local model caching is enabled in the inference service ConfigMap, lists cluster-scoped LocalModelCache and namespace-scoped LocalModelNamespaceCache resources to find one whose storage URI matches the service's model URI, then stamps matching local-model labels and PVC-name annotations onto the LLMInferenceService (namespace-scoped caches take precedence over cluster-scoped ones).

name: llminferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha2.validator
purpose: Validating admission webhook for the LLMInferenceService v1alpha2 custom resource that enforces structural and cross-field constraints on create and update: router/gateway/HTTPRoute consistency, parallelism configuration (pipeline vs data, worker requirements, immutability of total parallelism size), scheduler config (replicas, inline vs ref), LoRA adapter naming (uniqueness, path-traversal prevention, base-model collision), and autoscaling rules (replicas vs scaling mutual exclusivity, HPA/KEDA actuator selection, WVA variantCost format, decode/prefill actuator consistency, KEDA idleReplicaCount bounds).

name: llminferenceserviceconfig.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha1.validator
purpose: Validates LLMInferenceServiceConfig resources on create and update, ensuring baseRefs is not set (recursive refs are disabled), scheduler replicas are positive if specified, and running any injected controller-level validation. It also emits warnings when well-known configs are modified or deleted.

name: llminferenceserviceconfig.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha2.validator
purpose: Validates LLMInferenceServiceConfig resources on create and update, rejecting configs that use the forbidden baseRefs field (recursive refs are disabled) or specify invalid scheduler replicas (must be >0), and emits warnings when well-known configs are modified or deleted.

name: servingruntime.kserve-webhook-server.validator
purpose: Validates ServingRuntime and ClusterServingRuntime resources on create/update to ensure model format priority consistency (no duplicate priorities across runtimes for the same model format and protocol, and consistent priorities within a single runtime), and validates multi-node worker spec constraints including GPU resource types, parallel size values, blocked environment variables, and disallowing removal of an existing workerSpec.

purpose.name: llminferenceserviceconfig.kserve-webhook-server.v1alpha1.validator
purpose.purpose: Validates LocalModelNamespaceCache resources on create, update, and delete. On create/update, it ensures all referenced node groups exist; on delete, it prevents removal if the cache is still referenced by any InferenceService or LLMInferenceService via matching local-model labels.

operator_config.name: AddToScheme

AddToScheme adds all types of this clientset into the given scheme. This allows composition
of clientsets, like in:

	import (
	  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
	  clientsetscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	  aggregatorclientsetscheme "k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/client/clientset_generated/clientset/scheme"
	)

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

operator_config.doc:
An extra enum entry to prevent people from writing code that

Nobody should ever reference this enumeration entry. In particular,

operator_config.name: Code_FAILED_PRECONDITION
operator_config.doc:
Operation was rejected because the system is not in a state
required for the operation's execution.  For example, directory
to be deleted may be non-empty, an rmdir operation is applied to
a non-directory, etc.

A litmus test that may help a service implementor in deciding
between FAILED_PRECONDITION, ABORTED, and UNAVAILABLE:

	(a) Use UNAVAILABLE if the client can retry just the failing call.
	(b) Use ABORTED if the client should retry at a higher-level
	    (e.g., restarting a read-modify-write sequence).
	(c) Use FAILED_PRECONDITION if the client should not retry until
	    the system state has been explicitly fixed.  E.g., if an "rmdir"
	    fails because the directory is non-empty, FAILED_PRECONDITION
	    should be returned since the client should not retry unless
	    they have first fixed up the directory by deleting files from it.
	(d) Use FAILED_PRECONDITION if the client performs conditional
	    REST Get/Update/Delete on a resource and the resource on the
	    server does not match the condition. E.g., conflicting
	    read-modify-write on the same resource.

operator_config.name: Code_INTERNAL
operator_config.doc:
Internal errors.  Means some invariant expected by the underlying
system has been broken.  If you see one of these errors,
something is very broken.

operator_config.name: Code_INVALID_ARGUMENT
operator_config.doc:
Client specified an invalid argument.  Note that this differs
from FAILED_PRECONDITION.  INVALID_ARGUMENT indicates arguments
that are problematic regardless of the state of the system
(e.g., a malformed file name).

operator_config.name: Code_NOT_FOUND
operator_config.doc:
Some requested entity (e.g., file or directory) was not found.
For privacy reasons, this code *may* be returned when the client
does not have the access right to the entity.

operator_config.name: Code_OK
operator_config.doc: Not an error; returned on success

operator_config.name: Code_OUT_OF_RANGE
operator_config.doc:
Operation tried to iterate past the valid input range.  E.g., seeking or
reading past end of file.

Unlike INVALID_ARGUMENT, this error indicates a problem that may
be fixed if the system state changes. For example, a 32-bit file
system will generate INVALID_ARGUMENT if asked to read at an
offset that is not in the range [0,2^32-1], but it will generate
OUT_OF_RANGE if asked to read from an offset past the current
file size.

There is a fair bit of overlap between FAILED_PRECONDITION and
OUT_OF_RANGE.  We recommend using OUT_OF_RANGE (the more specific
error) when it applies so that callers who are iterating through
a space can easily look for an OUT_OF_RANGE error to detect when
they are done.

operator_config.name: Code_PERMISSION_DENIED
operator_config.doc:
The caller does not have permission to execute the specified
operation.  PERMISSION_DENIED must not be used for rejections
caused by exhausting some resource (use RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
instead for those errors).  PERMISSION_DENIED must not be
used if the caller can not be identified (use UNAUTHENTICATED
instead for those errors).

operator_config.name: Code_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
operator_config.doc:
Some resource has been exhausted, perhaps a per-user quota, or

operator_config.name: Code_UNAUTHENTICATED
operator_config.doc:
The request does not have valid authentication credentials for the
operation.

operator_config.name: Code_UNAVAILABLE
operator_config.doc:
The service is currently unavailable.  This is a most likely a
transient condition and may be corrected by retrying with
a backoff.

See litmus test above for deciding between FAILED_PRECONDITION,
ABORTED, and UNAVAILABLE.
